name: Equestrian Committee Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  NOVEMBER 18, 2024

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER
  A regular meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
  called to order by CHAIR SCHACHTER at 7:01 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall.

  2.  ROLL CALL
  Committee Members Present:  Brtis, Griggs, Harik, Shinn, Silvano, Romanelli,
  Schachter, and Martin (joined at 7:05 pm)
  Committee Members Absent:  Nilsen, Pope
  City Staff Present:  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas

  3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  A.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 23, 2024

  MEMBER SILVANO moved, seconded by MEMBER GRIGGS to:

  APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES  OF  SEPTEMBER  23,  2024,
  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

  4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

  Community Member Ashley Copp provided public comment regarding slurry-
  coated streets on East Lariat Lane and Empty Saddle Club Lane stating that they
  should be assessed to reduce the risk of horses slipping. Ms. Copp also
  commented on the Nixle Alert system noting it usefulness and the frequency of
  the alerts. She requested Nixle notifications regarding trail closures be sent out
  more frequently when possible and that they include information regarding
  alternate trails. Ms. Copp also made public comment regarding the speed of traffic
  on Rolling Hills Road and visibility of the crosswalk. She requested that the City
  consider implementing additional safety measures in that area to draw attention to
  the crosswalk and that the issue be brought to the attention of the Traffic and
  Safety Committee.
  COMMITTEE MEMBER MARTIN joined the meeting at 7:05 p.m.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES  1
November 18, 2024
   CHAIR SCHACHTER thanked Ms. Copp for bringing the items to the Committee’s
  attention and stated that these items would be returned for further discussion.
  Supervisor Pinuelas added that staff would forward the information provided to
  Public Works staff.

  5.  STAFF REPORTS

  A.  CITY CELEBRATION DEBRIEF (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the item (as per the agenda
  material).

  She stated that the report had been shared with the City Council at its meeting of
  November 12, 2024. Supervisor Pinuelas reported that attendance appeared to be
  significantly higher than in past years and that all activities were available the entire
  time of the event this year. She also reported that the Gymkhana events continued
  to be popular and that the reintroduction of the Palos Verdes Peninsula Horsemen’s
  Association’s Poker Ride was well received.

  Discussion ensued regarding the attendance and the favorable weather that day.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER thanked the staff for their work and MEMBERS SHINN,
  HARIK, AND MARTIN for all their help.

  B.  PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER RESTROOM PROJECT UPDATE
  (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the item. She reported that the
  Post Closure Land Use Plan was submitted to the Los Angeles County Public
  Health Department Local Enforcement Agency on August 21 and that a response
  letter had been received outlining additional steps needed for full approval,
  including installation of methane monitoring systems around the perimeter and at
  the enclosed restroom. She reported that the City would be meeting later that week
  with various County Departments to better understand the additional requirements
  and to provide the additional information being requested.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that Supervisor Hahn’s office has been supportive in
  helping ensure the request keeps moving forward through the process, in response
  to MEMBER SHINN.

  C.  EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

  NONE.

  D.  MATTERS OF INTEREST

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES  2
November 18, 2024
   Supervisor Pinuelas stated that staff had no matters of interest to report.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER inquired about a eucalyptus tree at Chandler Park that is
  slated for removal. Superintendent Goldsmith responded that it was on the
  schedule and should be removed soon.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that staff would address the broken gate latch at
  Chandler Park in response to MEMBER GRIGGS.

  7.  COMMITTEE REPORTS

  A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL (VERBAL REPORT)

  In response to the audience member item, Superintendent Goldsmith stated that
  he is aware of the issue on East Lariat Lane and Empty Saddle Club Lane and
  noted that they are private streets.

  MEMBER GRIGGS expressed concern about crossing at Mason Gate and inquired
  about additional measures to slow traffic such as reflectors. Superintendent
  Goldsmith responded that the radar sign could be placed over there.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER shared that the Traffic and Safety Committee is meeting on
  Wednesday of that week at 6:00 pm, where these issues can be shared under
  audience items to that Committee.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated staff would put a speed radar sign in that Rolling
  Hills Road and that striping requests would need to be reviewed by the Traffic and
  Safety Committee, in response to Ms. Copp.

  MEMBER SHINN suggested having the Sheriff Department in the area during high
  traffic times to monitor speeds.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  MEMBER GRIGGS referenced the recent Mountain Fire in Camarillo and inquired
  about agendizing an item to discuss allowing horse owners to keep horse trailers
  on their property so they can evacuate their horses in emergency situations.

  Discussion ensued regarding the municipal code regarding trailers, how to get the
  horses evacuated, and special parking permits issued during construction.

  Supervisor Pinuelas suggested the item first be discussed at the next Equine
  Emergency Preparedness Subcommittee meeting and that next steps could be
  determined at that time.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES  3
November 18, 2024
   MEMBER MARTIN expressed concern about lessons and clinics and inquired
  about arena limits at Ernie Howlett Park. Supervisor Pinuelas responded that there
  are no student limits set for the arenas at Ernie Howlett Park and noted that there
  are time limits for lessons.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that there is a two-hour time limit for consecutive
  lessons in the arenas which requires trainers to exit the arena for one hour before
  resuming lessons in response to CHAIR SCHACHTER.

  MEMBER SILVANO requested the item be added to the next agenda for further
  discussion and inquired about the cost of the daily license. Supervisor Pinuelas
  responded that the cost is $30 per day.

  Discussion ensued regarding clinics versus lessons, the cost of arena rental, and
  participant costs for clinics.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER directed staff to add an item to the next agenda to review the
  arena rules and discuss defining clinics and lessons.

  9.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR SCHACHTER ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:30 p.m.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  __________________________
  Rosa Pinuelas  Pam Brown Schachter
  Community Services Supervisor  Chair

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES  4
November 18, 2024
